articles.headline: Former Man City boss Roberto Mancini: Unconcerned by guilty verdict
articles.description: Former Manchester City manager and current Italy coach Roberto Mancini says he is unconcerned about being implicated in the financial rule-breaking scandal engulfing the English club, which on Friday said it was appealing the verdict.
articles.body:
ROME -- Former Manchester City manager and current Italy coach Roberto Mancini says he is unconcerned about being implicated in the financial rule-breaking scandal engulfing the English club, which on Friday said it was appealing the verdict.

In his latest comments on the issue, Mancini said: "It's not a problem that concerns me" -- despite appearing to acknowledge last weekend before a Nations League match in Turkey that he had "a double contract" as City coach from 2009-13.

Among the raft of charges that City has faced is an alleged failure to provide accurate details for player and manager payments between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

In 2018, German magazine Der Spiegel published evidence showing Mancini doubled his base salary of £1.45 million (now $1.9 million) for advising a club in Abu Dhabi.

City has been accused of potentially avoiding paying about £12 million ($16 million) in income tax and national insurance in relation to Mancini's salary, The Telegraph reported this week.

Mancini was asked if he was worried about the case ahead of Italy's match in France on Friday.

"No. I already spoke it about the other night. It's not something that concerns me. It's City's problem, unfortunately," Mancini said late Thursday at the Stade de France.

"It's not a problem that concerns me," Mancini added, repeating himself. "Look, really. I already said it the other day in Turkey."

- How Man City players, staff are handling Premier League verdict

- Man City appeal guilty verdict in Premier League breaches case

- Manchester City guilty charges explained: Premier League's options, how appeal works, more

In Turkey, Mancini said that "Manchester City is not guilty and the fact of having a double contract isn't my problem but theirs, probably."

Mancini led City to its first titles after Abu Dhabi's ruling family had bought the club in 2008, winning the FA Cup in 2011 and in 2011-12 coaching the team to its first Premier League title in a half century.

He was fired days after a shocking loss to Wigan in the FA Cup final in 2013.

City has protested its innocence throughout the long-running case, which reached a milestone Tuesday when the Premier League published a verdict saying the club was "guilty of all charges related to serious breaches" of the competition's financial rules from 2009-18.

articles.headline: Browns DT Mason Graham set to miss a few weeks, sources say
articles.description: Browns defensive tackle Mason Graham is expected to miss a few weeks after suffering an MCL sprain and ankle sprain against the Steelers, sources told NFL Network.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns defensive tackle Mason Graham is expected to miss a few weeks after suffering an MCL sprain and ankle sprain against the Pittsburgh Steelers, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport on Friday.

Graham sustained the injury during Pittsburgh's opening series Thursday night, as his left leg bent awkwardly while he was being blocked. Graham walked to the medical tent with some assistance before walking to the locker room.

Following the Browns' 27-24 win, Graham left the locker room on crutches and wearing a brace.

The No. 5 pick in the 2025 draft, Graham is off to a strong start to his second season. His four sacks lead the Browns and are tied for the second most in the NFL.

articles.headline: Tony Romo, CBS Sports agree to part after ex-QB's OWI arrest
articles.description: Tony Romo will not return as an NFL game analyst for CBS Sports, the network announced, after he was arrested in July on charges of operating a vehicle while intoxicated.
articles.body:
Tony Romo will not return as an NFL game analyst for CBS Sports, the network announced Friday, after he was arrested in July on charges of operating a vehicle while intoxicated.

"CBS Sports and Tony Romo have mutually agreed to part ways," the network said in a statement. "We thank Tony for his contributions over the past nine years and wish him the best moving forward."

The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback was arrested after a traffic stop in Milwaukee on July 23. Court records showed that one of the arresting officers said he detected a "strong odor of an alcoholic beverage" on Romo's breath. Romo performed poorly on field sobriety tests and was taken into custody and later released.

Romo pleaded no contest Sept. 1 and had his driving privileges revoked for six months. He was also ordered to have an ignition interlock device installed on any vehicle owned, registered or operated by him, attend and complete an alcohol assessment program, and pay a $784 fine.

CBS said J.J. Watt will continue to serve as the network's lead analyst, a role he took when Romo was placed on leave ahead of the season.

Romo said in a statement that he will take time off before considering his future.

"I'm proud of what I accomplished at CBS Sports over the last nine years. I approached my role as a game analyst the way I've approached everything in my life -- with a desire to win and be the best that I can be," Romo said. "I'm going to use this time to take a break, something I've never done before, and focus on my health and my family before moving on to my next opportunity. I am grateful for my time with CBS Sports and for the continued support of my family and friends, as well as the NFL community and fans."

Romo, 46, made four Pro Bowl appearances during an NFL career from 2004 to 2016 that was spent entirely with the Cowboys.

Following his no contest plea, Romo said in an Instagram post that the multiple back surgeries that led to his retirement as a player "left me with constant, debilitating pain." He noted that the pain "led to a dependence on pain medication, and my efforts to get off those medications led to an over-reliance on alcohol."

"None of this is an excuse," Romo said. "These are my failures and I take responsibility for them."

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

articles.headline: Jaguars' Coen: Hunter cares only about winning, not 'other stuff'
articles.description: How much Jaguars cornerback/receiver Travis Hunter is playing on defense and offense may be a subject of discussion among fans and analysts, but it definitely isn't inside the building.
articles.body:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- How much Jacksonville Jaguars cornerback/receiver Travis Hunter is playing on defense and offense might be a subject of discussion among fans and analysts, but it definitely isn't inside the building.

And it's not something Hunter talks about, either.

"He cares about winning," coach Liam Coen said. "That's what he cares about. And all the other stuff, the reps, where we picked him, I don't give two F's about value, and neither does he.

"We care about winning, and that's it."

Hunter, the No. 2 pick in the 2025 draft, started every game at cornerback this season but has played 62% of the team's defensive snaps because the Jaguars have a rotation with Jarrian Jones and Montaric Brown. Hunter recorded his first career interception in Sunday's 35-6 victory over New England.

He has played only 16 snaps on offense and has one catch for 8 yards and one carry for 3 yards. That's a significant drop-off from 2025 when Hunter played 67% of the Jaguars' offensive snaps in seven games before suffering a season-ending knee injury.

Sunday's game at Cincinnati will be a major test for Hunter and the Jaguars' secondary. The Bengals have arguably the NFL's best receiver duo in Ja'Marr Chase (18 catches, 185 yards, three TDs) and Tee Higgins (14 catches, 244 yards, one TD). Joe Burrow is completing 71% of his passes for 743 yards and six touchdowns.

"Just go out there and compete," Hunter said Thursday of his mindset going into the game. "Just be the best person I can be. And we've just got to go out there and do our job."

articles.headline: Erik Ten Hag 'was a piece of crap' with Man United squad - Fred
articles.description: Former Manchester United midfielder Fred has accused ex-boss Erik ten Hag of being a 'piece of crap' when it came to squad management.
articles.body:
Former Manchester United midfielder Fred has accused ex-boss Erik ten Hag of being a 'piece of crap' when it came to squad management.

The Brazilian spent five years at United, winning the League Cup and reaching the FA Cup final in the 2022-23 season.

Ten Hag came to United with a big reputation, having managed Ajax for four seasons and taking them to the Champions League semifinals but, while he did win the FA Cup and League Cup in his two-and-a-half years in Manchester, things did not quite go as planned with regards to success in the Premier League.

And Fred, who left the club to join Turkish side Fenerbahce during Ten Hag's tenure ahead of the 2023-24 season, gave a damning review of his time under the Dutchman.

"Ten Hag was tactically very good, but with the group he was a piece of crap," he said on the "Charla Podcast."

"He argued with everyone. He argued with me, with Cristiano [Ronaldo], with Casemiro, with Rashford ... He wouldn't put me in to play, sometimes it got stressful.

"[With Ten Hag] Only his Dutch players played. A clique-ridden coach. But, tactically, one of the best I've ever worked with.

- Sir Alex Ferguson on David Beckham's Preston loan: 'He thought I wanted him gone but that's not true'

- Sir Alex Ferguson was 'terrified' about Old Trafford return after brain surgery

- Rasmus Højlund hits 'Siuuu' against Portugal: 'Cristiano Ronaldo will never be forgotten'

"He wanted the team to run, but Cristiano [was already] older. He took Cristiano out [of the starting lineup], and then there was a falling out."

Ronaldo left the club at the end of the 2022 season after he found himself no longer in the starting lineup.

Ten Hag was sacked in October 2024, with United 14th after seven matches -- their worst start since the 1989-90 season.

Fred also lifted the lid on other United managers he experienced, including Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, the 1999 treble winner who took the helm at the club in December 2018 after Jose Mourinho was sacked.

The 33-year-old, who has 32 Brazil caps, gave his assessment of both of those managers, who he had much more positive things to say about.

"Solskjaer was good with the group, but he was helped [in training] by the assistants. He united the group," Fred added.

"Mourinho's a great bloke, he is funny. I've just been with him at Fenerbahçe; he brought me to United.

"Before [Carlo] Ancelotti came along, his name was being mentioned for the national team [Brazil].

"So I'd show him the rumours and he'd say: 'F--- off, mate. I'm not going anywhere. I'm going to manage my club here.' A really decent bloke."

articles.headline: Fantasy football buzz: How will absence of DeVonta Smith affect other Eagles?
articles.description: Philly's top wideout will miss Sunday's game. Matt Bowen provides pickup options and how to value other Eagles.
articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Oct. 2: What to expect from Eagles without DeVonta Smith

By Matt Bowen

With reports that a hamstring injury will keep Eagles wide receiver DeVonta Smith out of the lineup this Sunday in the home matchup against the Rams, let's discuss the fantasy implications for Philadelphia.

If you're a Smith manager, you can pivot to Dontayvion Wicks or Makai Lemon as streaming options, as both are available in slightly more than 50% of ESPN leagues. You can also check out the last-minute pickups column for a handful of other viable options at wide receiver.

Wicks scored 12 or more points in each of his first two games, catching a touchdown in Week 1. He has a big-play element to his game (19.9 YPC), so he will see more vertical opportunities on Sunday against a Rams defense that will mix both man and zone coverages. He can be played as a WR3/flex with more upside due to the third-level targets (seven targets of 15 or more air yards this season).

Lemon has seen only nine targets on the season, catching seven of them for 38 yards. However, the rookie has run 28 routes per game and his role should expand versus L.A. Going back to Lemon's college tape at USC, he can manipulate coverage at the top of the route, plus he accelerates thorough the ball. Those are good traits to have in this league. He should be viewed as a lower-tier WR3 for this matchup.

I would expect the Eagles to be more run-heavy in this game without Smith, which should put Saquon Barkley at 15-20 carries. Meanwhile, Jalen Hurts -- who was already outside of the top 10 QBs in our consensus ranks -- will have an even lower ceiling heading into Sunday. Yes, Hurts can provide a boost to the lineup due to his running ability, however he has scored only one rushing touchdown on the season while averaging 29 yards per game.

Oct. 2: You should be paying attention to Aaron Rodgers

By Adam Rank

At least for one night in Cleveland, Aaron Rodgers turned back the clock. Was it the 299 passing yards? The three touchdowns? Or the fact that I really believed that his desperation heave in the waning seconds of the game was going to find its way into the mitts of a Steelers receiver who would carry it into the end zone for a walk-off touchdown?

Sure, all of it.

Look, I make no apologies for being the supporter of a team that was on the losing side of "Rodgers magic" way too many times. However, I'm not going to lie when I tell you I was seriously nervous on that final throw. I've seen it too many times.
